question: Why does ice float in water? Please explain it simply in about 70 words.

response.message: Ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water. When water freezes, hydrogen bonds lock its molecules into a rigid, hexagonal lattice that holds them farther apart than in the liquid state. This open structure makes a given volume of ice weigh less than the same volume of liquid water. Since less dense substances float on denser liquids, ice stays at the surface rather than sinking[1](https://www.thoughtco.com/why-does-ice-float-604304)[3](https://www.fizzicseducation.com.au/150-science-experiments/polar-science/why-does-ice-float/).
